title: Inspect and extend: Demo wallet versus Electrum adapter
objective: Use the real implementation in `src/wallet-core.ts` to demonstrate and safely improve walletcore boundary, demowalletcore, electrumwalletcore, and websocket transport.
problem: An adapter lets the same screen ask different backends for wallet operations. Compare the local demo with the Electrum client and trace how context selects/wires it and how JSON-RPC messages travel. Your implementation or debugging result must remain consistent with the source architecture.
requirements: Read `src/wallet-core.ts` and the related project files: src/wallet-core.ts; src/persistence.ts; src/walletContext.tsx.
Add or improve a focused behavior related to walletcore boundary, demowalletcore, electrumwalletcore, and websocket transport.
Add a meaningful unit test or, when platform tooling is unavailable, document a reproducible manual check.
Update documentation to identify local, simulated, external, and missing behavior accurately.
constraints: Do not claim or implement as complete a capability outside this boundary: Source mismatch: the client constructs a React Native WebSocket but defaults to protocol ssl (and accepts tcp), neither of which is an accepted WebSocket URL scheme. A raw Electrum TCP/TLS endpoint needs a compatible WebSocket gateway or a different transport. The adapter also sends only when the socket is OPEN while calls can be issued immediately, so a first request may be silently dropped. No live Electrum connection was tested.
Do not add credentials, personal records, real funds, or unsafe public network exposure.
Keep the change within the existing project architecture and name any new dependencies.
expected_behavior: An adapter lets the same screen ask different backends for wallet operations. Compare the local demo with the Electrum client and trace how context selects/wires it and how JSON-RPC messages travel.
acceptance_criteria: The implementation change is traceable to `src/wallet-core.ts`.
Normal and failure/edge cases are described and tested.
The test outcome and environment are recorded honestly.
README or source comments correctly state remaining limitations.
hints: Read the caller and the closest existing test before editing.
Separate a pure rule test from any UI, device, provider, or network test.
